verses.display_text: Demetrius heard that Nicanor and his force had fallen in battle, and again sent Bacchides and Alcimus into the land of Judah, with the right wing of the army.

verses.display_text: They travelled the road to Gilgal, encamped against Mesaloth in Arbela, seized it, and destroyed many human lives.

verses.display_text: In the first month of the one hundred and fifty-second year they encamped against Jerusalem.

verses.text: They set out and went to Berea with twenty thousand men and two thousand cavalry.
verses.display_text: They set out and went to Berea with twenty thousand men and two thousand cavalry.

verses.text: Judas was encamped at Elasa with three thousand picked men.
verses.display_text: Judas was encamped at Elasa with three thousand picked men.

verses.display_text: They saw the multitude of the forces, how many they were, and became exceedingly afraid. Many slipped away from the camp, and only eight hundred men were left.

verses.display_text: Judas saw that his army had slipped away and that the battle was pressing upon him. His heart was crushed, because he had no time to gather them.

verses.display_text: He grew faint and said to those remaining, “Let us arise and go up against our adversaries, if perhaps we can fight them.”

verses.display_text: They tried to turn him back, saying, “We certainly cannot! Let us save our lives for now. We will return with our brothers and fight them, but we are few.”

verses.display_text: Judas said, “Far be it from us to do this thing and flee from them! If our time has drawn near, let us die courageously for our brothers and leave no charge against our glory.”

verses.display_text: The force moved out of the camp and took position to meet them. The cavalry was divided into two parts; the slingers and archers went ahead of the force, and all the foremost fighters were mighty men. Bacchides was on the right wing.

verses.display_text: The phalanx approached from both sides, and they sounded the trumpets. Judas’s men also sounded their trumpets.

verses.display_text: The earth was shaken by the sound of the armies, and battle was joined from morning until evening.

verses.text: Judas saw that Bacchides and the strongest part of the army were on the right. All who were courageous in heart gathered to him,

verses.display_text: Those on the left wing saw that the right wing had been crushed, and turned to follow on the heels of Judas and those with him from behind.

verses.display_text: The battle grew heavy, and many fell wounded on both sides.

verses.display_text: Judas fell, and the rest fled.

verses.display_text: Jonathan and Simon took up Judas their brother and buried him in the tomb of his fathers in Modein.

verses.text: They wept for him, and all Israel lamented him with a great lament. They mourned for many days and said,
verses.display_text: They wept for him, and all Israel lamented him with a great lament. They mourned for many days and said,

verses.text: “How has the mighty one fallen, the saviour of Israel!”
verses.display_text: “How has the mighty one fallen, the saviour of Israel!”

verses.text: The rest of the deeds of Judas, his battles, the brave deeds he performed, and his greatness were not written down, for they were exceedingly many.
verses.display_text: The rest of the deeds of Judas, his battles, the brave deeds he performed, and his greatness were not written down, for they were exceedingly many.

verses.text: After the death of Judas, the lawless emerged throughout all Israel’s territory, and all who practiced injustice rose up.
verses.display_text: After the death of Judas, the lawless emerged throughout all Israel’s territory, and all who practiced injustice rose up.

verses.text: In those days an exceedingly great famine occurred, and the country went over to their side.
verses.display_text: In those days an exceedingly great famine occurred, and the country went over to their side.

verses.text: Bacchides chose the ungodly men and appointed them masters of the country.
verses.display_text: Bacchides chose the ungodly men and appointed them masters of the country.

verses.text: They sought out and searched for Judas’s friends and brought them to Bacchides, who punished and mocked them.
verses.display_text: They sought out and searched for Judas’s friends and brought them to Bacchides, who punished and mocked them.

verses.text: Great distress came upon Israel, such as had not occurred since the day a prophet was no longer seen among them.
verses.display_text: Great distress came upon Israel, such as had not occurred since the day a prophet was no longer seen among them.

verses.text: All Judas’s friends gathered and said to Jonathan,
verses.display_text: All Judas’s friends gathered and said to Jonathan,

verses.text: “Since your brother Judas died, there is no man like him to go out and come in against our enemies, Bacchides, and those hostile to our nation.
verses.display_text: “Since your brother Judas died, there is no man like him to go out and come in against our enemies, Bacchides, and those hostile to our nation.

verses.text: Now, therefore, today we have chosen you to be our ruler and leader in his place, to fight our war.”
verses.display_text: Now, therefore, today we have chosen you to be our ruler and leader in his place, to fight our war.”

verses.text: Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time and arose in place of Judas his brother.
verses.display_text: Jonathan accepted the leadership at that time and arose in place of Judas his brother.

verses.text: Bacchides learned of it and sought to kill him.
verses.display_text: Bacchides learned of it and sought to kill him.

verses.text: Jonathan, Simon his brother, and all who were with him learned of it and fled into the wilderness of Tekoa. They encamped by the water of the pool of Asphar.
verses.display_text: Jonathan, Simon his brother, and all who were with him learned of it and fled into the wilderness of Tekoa. They encamped by the water of the pool of Asphar.

verses.text: Bacchides learned of it on the sabbath day, and he and his whole army came beyond the Jordan.
verses.display_text: Bacchides learned of it on the sabbath day, and he and his whole army came beyond the Jordan.

verses.text: Jonathan sent his brother, a leader of the company, and appealed to his friends the Nabateans to allow their many belongings to be deposited with them.
verses.display_text: Jonathan sent his brother, a leader of the company, and appealed to his friends the Nabateans to allow their many belongings to be deposited with them.

verses.display_text: The sons of Jambri from Medaba came out, seized John and everything he had, and went away with it.

verses.display_text: After these events they reported to Jonathan and Simon his brother, “The sons of Jambri are holding a great wedding and bringing the bride from Nadabath, the daughter of one of the great nobles of Canaan, with a great escort.”

verses.text: They remembered the blood of John their brother, went up, and hid under the cover of the mountain.
verses.display_text: They remembered the blood of John their brother, went up, and hid under the cover of the mountain.

verses.text: They raised their eyes and saw a commotion and much baggage. The bridegroom, his friends, and his brothers came out to meet them with tambourines, musicians, and many weapons.
verses.display_text: They raised their eyes and saw a commotion and much baggage. The bridegroom, his friends, and his brothers came out to meet them with tambourines, musicians, and many weapons.

verses.text: They rose against them from the ambush and killed them. Many fell wounded, and the survivors fled into the mountain. They took all their spoils.
verses.display_text: They rose against them from the ambush and killed them. Many fell wounded, and the survivors fled into the mountain. They took all their spoils.

verses.text: The wedding was turned into mourning, and the sound of their musicians into lamentation.
verses.display_text: The wedding was turned into mourning, and the sound of their musicians into lamentation.

verses.text: They exacted vengeance for their brother’s blood and returned to the marsh of the Jordan.
verses.display_text: They exacted vengeance for their brother’s blood and returned to the marsh of the Jordan.

verses.text: Bacchides heard and came on the sabbath day to the banks of the Jordan with a large force.
verses.display_text: Bacchides heard and came on the sabbath day to the banks of the Jordan with a large force.

verses.text: Jonathan said to his men, “Come, let us arise and fight for our lives, for today is not like yesterday or the day before.
verses.display_text: Jonathan said to his men, “Come, let us arise and fight for our lives, for today is not like yesterday or the day before.

verses.text: Behold! Battle is before us and behind us, the water of the Jordan is on either side, and there are marsh and thicket. There is nowhere to turn aside.
verses.display_text: Behold! Battle is before us and behind us, the water of the Jordan is on either side, and there are marsh and thicket. There is nowhere to turn aside.

verses.text: Now, therefore, cry out to Heaven so that you may be rescued from the hand of our enemies.”
verses.display_text: Now, therefore, cry out to Heaven so that you may be rescued from the hand of our enemies.”

verses.text: The battle was joined. Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, but he withdrew backward from him.
verses.display_text: The battle was joined. Jonathan stretched out his hand to strike Bacchides, but he withdrew backward from him.

verses.text: Jonathan and those with him leaped into the Jordan and swam across. The enemy did not cross the Jordan after them.
verses.display_text: Jonathan and those with him leaped into the Jordan and swam across. The enemy did not cross the Jordan after them.

verses.text: About a thousand of Bacchides’s men fell that day.
verses.display_text: About a thousand of Bacchides’s men fell that day.

verses.text: He returned to Jerusalem. They built fortified cities in Judea: the stronghold at Jericho, Emmaus, Beth-horon, Bethel, Thamnatha-Pharathon, and Tephon, with high walls, gates, and bars.
verses.display_text: He returned to Jerusalem. They built fortified cities in Judea: the stronghold at Jericho, Emmaus, Beth-horon, Bethel, Thamnatha-Pharathon, and Tephon, with high walls, gates, and bars.

verses.text: He placed garrisons in them to act against Israel.
verses.display_text: He placed garrisons in them to act against Israel.

verses.text: He fortified the city of Beth-zur, Gazara, and the citadel, and placed forces and stores of food in them.
verses.display_text: He fortified the city of Beth-zur, Gazara, and the citadel, and placed forces and stores of food in them.

verses.text: He took the sons of the leaders of the country as hostages and placed them under guard in the citadel at Jerusalem.
verses.display_text: He took the sons of the leaders of the country as hostages and placed them under guard in the citadel at Jerusalem.

verses.text: In the second month of the one hundred and fifty-third year, Alcimus ordered the wall of the inner court of the holy places to be demolished. He began tearing down the works of the prophets.
verses.display_text: In the second month of the one hundred and fifty-third year, Alcimus ordered the wall of the inner court of the holy places to be demolished. He began tearing down the works of the prophets.

verses.text: At that time Alcimus was struck, and his work was obstructed. His mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed, unable to speak another word or give orders concerning his household.
verses.display_text: At that time Alcimus was struck, and his work was obstructed. His mouth was stopped, and he was paralyzed, unable to speak another word or give orders concerning his household.

verses.text: Alcimus died at that time in great torment.
verses.display_text: Alcimus died at that time in great torment.

verses.text: Bacchides saw that Alcimus had died and returned to the king. The land of Judah was quiet for two years.
verses.display_text: Bacchides saw that Alcimus had died and returned to the king. The land of Judah was quiet for two years.

verses.text: All the lawless took counsel, saying, “Behold! Jonathan and his men are living quietly and confidently. Let us now bring up Bacchides, and he will seize them all in one night.”
verses.display_text: All the lawless took counsel, saying, “Behold! Jonathan and his men are living quietly and confidently. Let us now bring up Bacchides, and he will seize them all in one night.”

verses.text: They went and conferred with him.
verses.display_text: They went and conferred with him.

verses.text: He set out to come with a large force and secretly sent letters to all his allies in Judea to seize Jonathan and those with him. But they could not, because their plan had become known.
verses.display_text: He set out to come with a large force and secretly sent letters to all his allies in Judea to seize Jonathan and those with him. But they could not, because their plan had become known.

verses.text: Jonathan’s men seized about fifty men from the country who were ringleaders of the evil and killed them.
verses.display_text: Jonathan’s men seized about fifty men from the country who were ringleaders of the evil and killed them.

verses.text: Jonathan, Simon, and those with him withdrew to Beth-basi in the wilderness. He rebuilt its demolished parts, and they strengthened it.
verses.display_text: Jonathan, Simon, and those with him withdrew to Beth-basi in the wilderness. He rebuilt its demolished parts, and they strengthened it.

verses.text: Bacchides learned of it, gathered his whole multitude, and gave orders to those from Judea.
verses.display_text: Bacchides learned of it, gathered his whole multitude, and gave orders to those from Judea.

verses.text: He came, encamped against Beth-basi, attacked it for many days, and made siege engines.
verses.display_text: He came, encamped against Beth-basi, attacked it for many days, and made siege engines.

verses.text: Jonathan left Simon his brother in the city, went out into the country, and came with a small number.
verses.display_text: Jonathan left Simon his brother in the city, went out into the country, and came with a small number.

verses.text: He struck Odomera, his brothers, and the sons of Phasiron in their encampment. They began striking and advancing with their forces.
verses.display_text: He struck Odomera, his brothers, and the sons of Phasiron in their encampment. They began striking and advancing with their forces.

verses.text: Simon and those with him came out of the city and burned the siege engines.
verses.display_text: Simon and those with him came out of the city and burned the siege engines.

verses.text: They fought Bacchides, and he was crushed by them. They pressed him greatly, for his plan and his expedition had come to nothing.
verses.display_text: They fought Bacchides, and he was crushed by them. They pressed him greatly, for his plan and his expedition had come to nothing.

verses.text: He became furious with the lawless men who had advised him to come into the country, killed many of them, and resolved to depart to his own land.
verses.display_text: He became furious with the lawless men who had advised him to come into the country, killed many of them, and resolved to depart to his own land.

verses.text: Jonathan learned of it and sent envoys to him to arrange peace with him and to return the captives to them.
verses.display_text: Jonathan learned of it and sent envoys to him to arrange peace with him and to return the captives to them.

verses.text: He accepted and acted according to his words, and swore to him that he would not seek his harm all the days of his life.
verses.display_text: He accepted and acted according to his words, and swore to him that he would not seek his harm all the days of his life.

verses.text: He returned to him the captives he had previously taken from the land of Judah. He turned and went away to his own land and did not come again into their territory.
verses.display_text: He returned to him the captives he had previously taken from the land of Judah. He turned and went away to his own land and did not come again into their territory.

verses.text: The sword ceased from Israel. Jonathan settled in Michmash, began to judge the people, and removed the ungodly from Israel.
verses.display_text: The sword ceased from Israel. Jonathan settled in Michmash, began to judge the people, and removed the ungodly from Israel.

verses.text: In the one hundred and sixtieth year Alexander Epiphanes, son of Antiochus, came up and seized Ptolemais. They received him, and he reigned there.
verses.display_text: In the one hundred and sixtieth year Alexander Epiphanes, son of Antiochus, came up and seized Ptolemais. They received him, and he reigned there.

verses.text: King Demetrius heard of it, gathered very large forces, and went out to meet him in battle.
verses.display_text: King Demetrius heard of it, gathered very large forces, and went out to meet him in battle.

verses.text: Demetrius sent letters to Jonathan with peaceful words, intending to exalt him.
verses.display_text: Demetrius sent letters to Jonathan with peaceful words, intending to exalt him.

verses.text: For he said, “Let us be first to make peace with them before he makes an agreement with Alexander against us.
verses.display_text: For he said, “Let us be first to make peace with them before he makes an agreement with Alexander against us.

verses.text: He will remember all the evils we have committed against him, his brothers, and the nation.”
verses.display_text: He will remember all the evils we have committed against him, his brothers, and the nation.”

verses.text: He gave him authority to gather forces, prepare weapons, and be his ally. He ordered that the hostages in the citadel be handed over to him.
verses.display_text: He gave him authority to gather forces, prepare weapons, and be his ally. He ordered that the hostages in the citadel be handed over to him.

verses.text: Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letters in the hearing of all the people and those in the citadel.
verses.display_text: Jonathan came to Jerusalem and read the letters in the hearing of all the people and those in the citadel.

verses.text: They were greatly afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather a force.
verses.display_text: They were greatly afraid when they heard that the king had given him authority to gather a force.

verses.text: Those in the citadel handed over the hostages to Jonathan, and he returned them to their parents.
verses.display_text: Those in the citadel handed over the hostages to Jonathan, and he returned them to their parents.

verses.text: Jonathan settled in Jerusalem and began rebuilding and renewing the city.
verses.display_text: Jonathan settled in Jerusalem and began rebuilding and renewing the city.

verses.text: He told the workers to build the walls and the enclosure around Mount Zion with four-foot stones for fortification, and they did so.
verses.display_text: He told the workers to build the walls and the enclosure around Mount Zion with four-foot stones for fortification, and they did so.

verses.text: The foreigners in the strongholds that Bacchides had built fled.
verses.display_text: The foreigners in the strongholds that Bacchides had built fled.

verses.text: Each abandoned his place and went to his own land.
verses.display_text: Each abandoned his place and went to his own land.

verses.text: Only at Beth-zur did some who had abandoned the law and the decrees remain, for it was a place of refuge.
verses.display_text: Only at Beth-zur did some who had abandoned the law and the decrees remain, for it was a place of refuge.

verses.text: King Alexander heard all the promises Demetrius had sent Jonathan. They recounted to him the battles and brave deeds that he and his brothers had performed, and the hardships they had endured.
verses.display_text: King Alexander heard all the promises Demetrius had sent Jonathan. They recounted to him the battles and brave deeds that he and his brothers had performed, and the hardships they had endured.

verses.text: He said, “Could we find another man like this? Now we will make him our friend and ally.”
verses.display_text: He said, “Could we find another man like this? Now we will make him our friend and ally.”

verses.text: He wrote letters and sent them to him in these words:
verses.display_text: He wrote letters and sent them to him in these words:

verses.text: “King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.
verses.display_text: “King Alexander to his brother Jonathan, greetings.

verses.text: We have heard concerning you, that you are a man mighty in strength and suitable to be our friend.
verses.display_text: We have heard concerning you, that you are a man mighty in strength and suitable to be our friend.

verses.text: Now, therefore, today we have appointed you high priest of your nation and to be called the king’s Friend”—and he sent him a purple robe and a golden crown—“to be concerned for our interests and maintain friendship with us.”
verses.display_text: Now, therefore, today we have appointed you high priest of your nation and to be called the king’s Friend”—and he sent him a purple robe and a golden crown—“to be concerned for our interests and maintain friendship with us.”

verses.text: Jonathan put on the holy robe in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the Festival of Booths. He gathered forces and prepared many weapons.
verses.display_text: Jonathan put on the holy robe in the seventh month of the one hundred and sixtieth year, at the Festival of Booths. He gathered forces and prepared many weapons.

verses.text: Demetrius heard these things and was grieved. He said,
verses.display_text: Demetrius heard these things and was grieved. He said,

verses.text: “What have we done, that Alexander has anticipated us in securing friendship with the Jews for support?
verses.display_text: “What have we done, that Alexander has anticipated us in securing friendship with the Jews for support?

verses.text: I too will write them words of encouragement, honour, and gifts, so that they may be with me to help.”
verses.display_text: I too will write them words of encouragement, honour, and gifts, so that they may be with me to help.”

verses.text: He sent to them in these words: “King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
verses.display_text: He sent to them in these words: “King Demetrius to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

verses.text: We have heard that you have kept your agreements with us, remained in our friendship, and not joined our enemies, and we rejoiced.
verses.display_text: We have heard that you have kept your agreements with us, remained in our friendship, and not joined our enemies, and we rejoiced.

verses.text: Now continue to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good things for what you do with us.
verses.display_text: Now continue to keep faith with us, and we will repay you with good things for what you do with us.

verses.text: We will grant you many remissions and give you gifts.
verses.display_text: We will grant you many remissions and give you gifts.

verses.text: Now I release you and exempt all the Jews from tribute, the salt charge, and crown payments.
verses.display_text: Now I release you and exempt all the Jews from tribute, the salt charge, and crown payments.

verses.text: I relinquish from today onward the right to receive the third of the grain crop and the half of the fruit of the trees that fall to me, from the land of Judah and the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.
verses.display_text: I relinquish from today onward the right to receive the third of the grain crop and the half of the fruit of the trees that fall to me, from the land of Judah and the three districts added to it from Samaria and Galilee, from this day and for all time.

verses.text: Let Jerusalem and its territory be holy and exempt, free of tithes and dues.
verses.display_text: Let Jerusalem and its territory be holy and exempt, free of tithes and dues.

verses.text: I also relinquish authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men of his own choosing to guard it.
verses.display_text: I also relinquish authority over the citadel in Jerusalem and give it to the high priest, so that he may appoint in it men of his own choosing to guard it.

verses.text: Every Jewish person taken captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom I release freely, without payment. Let all remit their taxes, including those upon their livestock.
verses.display_text: Every Jewish person taken captive from the land of Judah into any part of my kingdom I release freely, without payment. Let all remit their taxes, including those upon their livestock.

verses.text: Let all festivals, sabbaths, new moons, and appointed days, and the three days before a festival and the three after it, all be days of exemption and release for all Jews in my kingdom.
verses.display_text: Let all festivals, sabbaths, new moons, and appointed days, and the three days before a festival and the three after it, all be days of exemption and release for all Jews in my kingdom.

verses.text: No one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.
verses.display_text: No one shall have authority to exact payment from or trouble any of them concerning any matter.

verses.text: Let up to thirty thousand men of the Jews be enrolled in the king’s forces, and let allowances be given to them, as is proper for all the king’s forces.
verses.display_text: Let up to thirty thousand men of the Jews be enrolled in the king’s forces, and let allowances be given to them, as is proper for all the king’s forces.

verses.text: Some of them shall be stationed in the king’s great strongholds, and some shall be appointed to positions of trust in the kingdom. Their supervisors and commanders shall be from among them, and they shall follow their own laws, as the king has also decreed in the land of Judah.
verses.display_text: Some of them shall be stationed in the king’s great strongholds, and some shall be appointed to positions of trust in the kingdom. Their supervisors and commanders shall be from among them, and they shall follow their own laws, as the king has also decreed in the land of Judah.

verses.text: Let the three districts added to Judea from the region of Samaria be attached to Judea, so that they may be reckoned under one authority and obey no other authority except the high priest.
verses.display_text: Let the three districts added to Judea from the region of Samaria be attached to Judea, so that they may be reckoned under one authority and obey no other authority except the high priest.

verses.text: I have given Ptolemais and the territory belonging to it as a gift to the holy places in Jerusalem, for the expenses proper to the holy places.
verses.display_text: I have given Ptolemais and the territory belonging to it as a gift to the holy places in Jerusalem, for the expenses proper to the holy places.

verses.text: I myself give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s accounts, from the appropriate places.
verses.display_text: I myself give every year fifteen thousand shekels of silver from the king’s accounts, from the appropriate places.

verses.text: All the excess that they did not pay from the revenues as in former years they shall from now on give for the works of the house.
verses.display_text: All the excess that they did not pay from the revenues as in former years they shall from now on give for the works of the house.

verses.text: Besides these, the five thousand shekels of silver that they used to take from the revenues of the holy place from its account each year are also remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.
verses.display_text: Besides these, the five thousand shekels of silver that they used to take from the revenues of the holy place from its account each year are also remitted, because they belong to the priests who minister.

verses.text: All who flee to the temple in Jerusalem and anywhere within its precincts, owing royal dues or any other obligation, shall be released, together with all they possess in my kingdom.
verses.display_text: All who flee to the temple in Jerusalem and anywhere within its precincts, owing royal dues or any other obligation, shall be released, together with all they possess in my kingdom.

verses.display_text: The cost of rebuilding and renewing the works of the holy places shall be given from the king’s account.

verses.display_text: The cost of rebuilding Jerusalem’s walls and fortifying it all around shall be given from the king’s account, and likewise for rebuilding walls in Judea.”

verses.text: When Jonathan and the people heard these words, they neither believed nor accepted them, because they remembered the great evil he had committed in Israel and how severely he had oppressed them.
verses.display_text: When Jonathan and the people heard these words, they neither believed nor accepted them, because they remembered the great evil he had committed in Israel and how severely he had oppressed them.

verses.text: They favoured Alexander, because he had been the first to speak peaceful words to them, and they remained his allies all his days.
verses.display_text: They favoured Alexander, because he had been the first to speak peaceful words to them, and they remained his allies all his days.

verses.text: King Alexander gathered great forces and encamped opposite Demetrius.
verses.display_text: King Alexander gathered great forces and encamped opposite Demetrius.

verses.text: The two kings joined battle. Demetrius’s army fled; Alexander pursued him and prevailed against them.
verses.display_text: The two kings joined battle. Demetrius’s army fled; Alexander pursued him and prevailed against them.

verses.text: He pressed the battle fiercely until the sun went down, and Demetrius fell that day.
verses.display_text: He pressed the battle fiercely until the sun went down, and Demetrius fell that day.

verses.text: Alexander sent envoys to Ptolemy king of Egypt in these words:
verses.display_text: Alexander sent envoys to Ptolemy king of Egypt in these words:

verses.text: “I have returned to my kingdom, sat upon the throne of my fathers, and taken control of the government. I have crushed Demetrius and gained control of our country.
verses.display_text: “I have returned to my kingdom, sat upon the throne of my fathers, and taken control of the government. I have crushed Demetrius and gained control of our country.

verses.text: I joined battle with him, and he and his army were crushed by us. We have sat upon the throne of his kingdom.
verses.display_text: I joined battle with him, and he and his army were crushed by us. We have sat upon the throne of his kingdom.

verses.text: Now let us establish friendship with one another. Give me your daughter as wife, and I will become your son-in-law and give you and her gifts worthy of you.”
verses.display_text: Now let us establish friendship with one another. Give me your daughter as wife, and I will become your son-in-law and give you and her gifts worthy of you.”

verses.text: King Ptolemy answered, saying, “The day you returned to the land of your fathers and sat upon the throne of their kingdom was a good day.
verses.display_text: King Ptolemy answered, saying, “The day you returned to the land of your fathers and sat upon the throne of their kingdom was a good day.

verses.text: Now I will do for you what you have written. But meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I will form a marriage alliance with you as you have said.”
verses.display_text: Now I will do for you what you have written. But meet me at Ptolemais, so that we may see one another, and I will form a marriage alliance with you as you have said.”

verses.text: Ptolemy left Egypt with Cleopatra his daughter and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.
verses.display_text: Ptolemy left Egypt with Cleopatra his daughter and came to Ptolemais in the one hundred and sixty-second year.

verses.text: King Alexander met him, and he gave him Cleopatra his daughter in marriage and celebrated her wedding at Ptolemais with great glory, as kings do.
verses.display_text: King Alexander met him, and he gave him Cleopatra his daughter in marriage and celebrated her wedding at Ptolemais with great glory, as kings do.

verses.text: King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come and meet him.
verses.display_text: King Alexander wrote to Jonathan to come and meet him.

verses.text: He went in honour to Ptolemais and met the two kings. He gave them and their Friends silver, gold, and many gifts, and found favour before them.
verses.display_text: He went in honour to Ptolemais and met the two kings. He gave them and their Friends silver, gold, and many gifts, and found favour before them.

verses.text: Pestilent men from Israel, lawless men, gathered against him to petition against him, but the king paid no attention to them.
verses.display_text: Pestilent men from Israel, lawless men, gathered against him to petition against him, but the king paid no attention to them.

verses.text: The king ordered them to remove Jonathan’s garments and clothe him in purple, and they did so.
verses.display_text: The king ordered them to remove Jonathan’s garments and clothe him in purple, and they did so.

verses.text: The king seated him with himself and said to his commanders, “Go out with him into the midst of the city and proclaim that no one may petition against him concerning any matter, and that no one may trouble him concerning any charge.”
verses.display_text: The king seated him with himself and said to his commanders, “Go out with him into the midst of the city and proclaim that no one may petition against him concerning any matter, and that no one may trouble him concerning any charge.”

verses.text: When the accusers saw his honour as proclaimed and saw him clothed in purple, they all fled.
verses.display_text: When the accusers saw his honour as proclaimed and saw him clothed in purple, they all fled.

verses.text: The king honoured him, enrolled him among the First Friends, and appointed him general and district governor.
verses.display_text: The king honoured him, enrolled him among the First Friends, and appointed him general and district governor.

verses.text: Jonathan returned to Jerusalem in peace and gladness.
verses.display_text: Jonathan returned to Jerusalem in peace and gladness.

verses.text: In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius son of Demetrius came from Crete into the land of his fathers.
verses.display_text: In the one hundred and sixty-fifth year, Demetrius son of Demetrius came from Crete into the land of his fathers.

verses.text: King Alexander heard of it, was greatly distressed, and returned to Antioch.
verses.display_text: King Alexander heard of it, was greatly distressed, and returned to Antioch.

verses.text: Demetrius appointed Apollonius, who was over Coele-Syria. He gathered a great force and encamped against Jamnia, and sent to Jonathan the high priest, saying,
verses.display_text: Demetrius appointed Apollonius, who was over Coele-Syria. He gathered a great force and encamped against Jamnia, and sent to Jonathan the high priest, saying,

verses.text: “You alone are raising yourself against us, and because of you I have become an object of ridicule and reproach. Why are you exercising power against us in the mountains?
verses.display_text: “You alone are raising yourself against us, and because of you I have become an object of ridicule and reproach. Why are you exercising power against us in the mountains?

verses.text: Now, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us measure ourselves against one another there, for a force from the cities is with me.
verses.display_text: Now, if you trust in your forces, come down to us into the plain, and let us measure ourselves against one another there, for a force from the cities is with me.

verses.text: Ask and learn who I am and who the others helping us are. They say, ‘There is no foothold for you before us, because your fathers were routed twice in their own land.’
verses.display_text: Ask and learn who I am and who the others helping us are. They say, ‘There is no foothold for you before us, because your fathers were routed twice in their own land.’

verses.text: Now you shall not be able to stand against the cavalry and such a force in the plain, where there is neither stone nor pebble nor a place to flee.”
verses.display_text: Now you shall not be able to stand against the cavalry and such a force in the plain, where there is neither stone nor pebble nor a place to flee.”

verses.text: When Jonathan heard Apollonius’s words, he was stirred in mind. He chose ten thousand men and went out from Jerusalem; Simon his brother met him to help him.
verses.display_text: When Jonathan heard Apollonius’s words, he was stirred in mind. He chose ten thousand men and went out from Jerusalem; Simon his brother met him to help him.

verses.text: He encamped against Joppa. The people of the city shut it against him, because Apollonius’s garrison was in Joppa, and they attacked it.
verses.display_text: He encamped against Joppa. The people of the city shut it against him, because Apollonius’s garrison was in Joppa, and they attacked it.

verses.text: The people of the city became afraid and opened it, and Jonathan gained control of Joppa.
verses.display_text: The people of the city became afraid and opened it, and Jonathan gained control of Joppa.

verses.text: Apollonius heard and brought three thousand cavalry and a large force into camp. He went toward Azotus as though passing through, while drawing forward into the plain because he had many cavalry and trusted in them.
verses.display_text: Apollonius heard and brought three thousand cavalry and a large force into camp. He went toward Azotus as though passing through, while drawing forward into the plain because he had many cavalry and trusted in them.

verses.text: Jonathan pursued him toward Azotus, and the armies joined battle.
verses.display_text: Jonathan pursued him toward Azotus, and the armies joined battle.

verses.text: Apollonius had secretly left a thousand cavalry behind them.
verses.display_text: Apollonius had secretly left a thousand cavalry behind them.

verses.text: Jonathan realized there was an ambush behind him. They surrounded his army and hurled missiles at the people from morning until evening.
verses.display_text: Jonathan realized there was an ambush behind him. They surrounded his army and hurled missiles at the people from morning until evening.

verses.text: But the people stood firm, as Jonathan had commanded, and their enemies’ horses grew weary.
verses.display_text: But the people stood firm, as Jonathan had commanded, and their enemies’ horses grew weary.

verses.text: Simon drew out his force and engaged the phalanx, for the cavalry was exhausted. They were crushed by him and fled,
verses.display_text: Simon drew out his force and engaged the phalanx, for the cavalry was exhausted. They were crushed by him and fled,

verses.text: and the cavalry scattered in the plain. They fled into Azotus and entered Beth-dagon, their idol shrine, for safety.
verses.display_text: and the cavalry scattered in the plain. They fled into Azotus and entered Beth-dagon, their idol shrine, for safety.

verses.text: Jonathan burned Azotus and its surrounding towns and took their spoils. He burned the temple of Dagon and those who had fled into it with fire.
verses.display_text: Jonathan burned Azotus and its surrounding towns and took their spoils. He burned the temple of Dagon and those who had fled into it with fire.

verses.text: Those who had fallen by the sword, together with those burned, numbered about eight thousand men.
verses.display_text: Those who had fallen by the sword, together with those burned, numbered about eight thousand men.

verses.text: Jonathan set out from there and encamped against Ascalon. The people of the city came out to meet him with great honour.
verses.display_text: Jonathan set out from there and encamped against Ascalon. The people of the city came out to meet him with great honour.

verses.text: Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with his men, carrying many spoils.
verses.display_text: Jonathan returned to Jerusalem with his men, carrying many spoils.

verses.text: When King Alexander heard these things, he honoured Jonathan still more.
verses.display_text: When King Alexander heard these things, he honoured Jonathan still more.

verses.text: He sent him a golden clasp, as is customarily given to the king’s Kinsmen, and gave him Ekron and all its territory as an inheritance.
verses.display_text: He sent him a golden clasp, as is customarily given to the king’s Kinsmen, and gave him Ekron and all its territory as an inheritance.

verses.text: The king of Egypt gathered many forces, like the sand beside the seashore, and many ships. He sought to gain control of Alexander’s kingdom by deceit and add it to his own kingdom.
verses.display_text: The king of Egypt gathered many forces, like the sand beside the seashore, and many ships. He sought to gain control of Alexander’s kingdom by deceit and add it to his own kingdom.

verses.text: He went out to Syria with peaceful words. The people of the cities opened to him and met him, because King Alexander had commanded them to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.
verses.display_text: He went out to Syria with peaceful words. The people of the cities opened to him and met him, because King Alexander had commanded them to meet him, since he was his father-in-law.

verses.text: As Ptolemy entered the cities, he stationed forces as a garrison in each city.
verses.display_text: As Ptolemy entered the cities, he stationed forces as a garrison in each city.

verses.text: When they approached Azotus, they showed him the burned temple of Dagon, Azotus and its surrounding towns demolished, the bodies thrown out, and those whom Jonathan had burned in the war. They had piled them in heaps along his route.
verses.display_text: When they approached Azotus, they showed him the burned temple of Dagon, Azotus and its surrounding towns demolished, the bodies thrown out, and those whom Jonathan had burned in the war. They had piled them in heaps along his route.

verses.text: They recounted to the king what Jonathan had done, to bring blame upon him. But the king remained silent.
verses.display_text: They recounted to the king what Jonathan had done, to bring blame upon him. But the king remained silent.

verses.text: Jonathan met the king at Joppa with honour. They greeted one another and lodged there.
verses.display_text: Jonathan met the king at Joppa with honour. They greeted one another and lodged there.

verses.text: Jonathan accompanied the king as far as the river called Eleutherus, then returned to Jerusalem.
verses.display_text: Jonathan accompanied the king as far as the river called Eleutherus, then returned to Jerusalem.

verses.text: King Ptolemy gained control of the coastal cities as far as Seleucia by the sea, and devised evil plans concerning Alexander.
verses.display_text: King Ptolemy gained control of the coastal cities as far as Seleucia by the sea, and devised evil plans concerning Alexander.

verses.text: He sent envoys to King Demetrius, saying, “Come, let us make a covenant with one another, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander had, and you shall reign over your father’s kingdom.
verses.display_text: He sent envoys to King Demetrius, saying, “Come, let us make a covenant with one another, and I will give you my daughter whom Alexander had, and you shall reign over your father’s kingdom.

verses.text: For I regret giving him my daughter, because he sought to kill me.”
verses.display_text: For I regret giving him my daughter, because he sought to kill me.”

verses.text: He accused him because he desired his kingdom.
verses.display_text: He accused him because he desired his kingdom.

verses.text: He took his daughter away from him, gave her to Demetrius, and became estranged from Alexander; their hostility became evident.
verses.display_text: He took his daughter away from him, gave her to Demetrius, and became estranged from Alexander; their hostility became evident.

verses.text: Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the diadem of Asia. He placed two diadems on his head, that of Egypt and that of Asia.
verses.display_text: Ptolemy entered Antioch and put on the diadem of Asia. He placed two diadems on his head, that of Egypt and that of Asia.

verses.text: King Alexander was in Cilicia at that time, because the people of those places were in revolt.
verses.display_text: King Alexander was in Cilicia at that time, because the people of those places were in revolt.

verses.text: Alexander heard and came against him in battle. Ptolemy led out his forces, met him with a strong force, and routed him.
verses.display_text: Alexander heard and came against him in battle. Ptolemy led out his forces, met him with a strong force, and routed him.

verses.text: Alexander fled into Arabia to find shelter there, and King Ptolemy was exalted.
verses.display_text: Alexander fled into Arabia to find shelter there, and King Ptolemy was exalted.

verses.text: Zabdiel the Arab cut off Alexander’s head and sent it to Ptolemy.
verses.display_text: Zabdiel the Arab cut off Alexander’s head and sent it to Ptolemy.

verses.text: King Ptolemy died on the third day, and his men in the strongholds were destroyed by those in the strongholds.
verses.display_text: King Ptolemy died on the third day, and his men in the strongholds were destroyed by those in the strongholds.

verses.text: Demetrius became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.
verses.display_text: Demetrius became king in the one hundred and sixty-seventh year.

verses.text: In those days Jonathan gathered the men of Judea to make war on the citadel in Jerusalem, and he made many siege engines against it.
verses.display_text: In those days Jonathan gathered the men of Judea to make war on the citadel in Jerusalem, and he made many siege engines against it.

verses.text: Some lawless men who hated their own nation went to the king and reported to him that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.
verses.display_text: Some lawless men who hated their own nation went to the king and reported to him that Jonathan was besieging the citadel.

verses.text: When he heard, he became angry. Immediately on hearing it he set out and came to Ptolemais. He wrote to Jonathan to stop the siege and to come as quickly as possible to confer with him at Ptolemais.
verses.display_text: When he heard, he became angry. Immediately on hearing it he set out and came to Ptolemais. He wrote to Jonathan to stop the siege and to come as quickly as possible to confer with him at Ptolemais.

verses.text: When Jonathan heard, he ordered the siege to continue, selected some elders of Israel and priests, and exposed himself to danger.
verses.display_text: When Jonathan heard, he ordered the siege to continue, selected some elders of Israel and priests, and exposed himself to danger.

verses.text: He took silver, gold, clothing, and many other gifts, went to the king at Ptolemais, and found favour before him.
verses.display_text: He took silver, gold, clothing, and many other gifts, went to the king at Ptolemais, and found favour before him.

verses.text: Some lawless men from the nation were petitioning against him.
verses.display_text: Some lawless men from the nation were petitioning against him.

verses.text: The king treated him as those before him had done and exalted him before all his Friends.
verses.display_text: The king treated him as those before him had done and exalted him before all his Friends.

verses.text: He confirmed him in the high priesthood and all the other honours he had held before, and made him rank among the First Friends.
verses.display_text: He confirmed him in the high priesthood and all the other honours he had held before, and made him rank among the First Friends.

verses.text: Jonathan asked the king to make Judea, the three districts, and Samaria free from tribute, and promised him three hundred talents.
verses.display_text: Jonathan asked the king to make Judea, the three districts, and Samaria free from tribute, and promised him three hundred talents.

verses.text: The king consented and wrote letters to Jonathan concerning all these things in the following form:
verses.display_text: The king consented and wrote letters to Jonathan concerning all these things in the following form:

verses.text: “King Demetrius to Jonathan his brother and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.
verses.display_text: “King Demetrius to Jonathan his brother and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

verses.text: We have also written to you a copy of the letter we wrote about you to Lasthenes our Kinsman, so that you may know it.
verses.display_text: We have also written to you a copy of the letter we wrote about you to Lasthenes our Kinsman, so that you may know it.

verses.text: ‘King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.
verses.display_text: ‘King Demetrius to Lasthenes his father, greetings.

verses.text: We have judged it good to benefit the nation of the Jews, our friends who keep their obligations toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.
verses.display_text: We have judged it good to benefit the nation of the Jews, our friends who keep their obligations toward us, because of their goodwill toward us.

verses.text: We have confirmed to them the territory of Judea and the three districts of Aphairema, Lydda, and Rathamin, added to Judea from Samaria, with everything belonging to them, for all who sacrifice in Jerusalem, in place of the royal dues that the king formerly received from them each year from the produce of the land and the fruit trees.
verses.display_text: We have confirmed to them the territory of Judea and the three districts of Aphairema, Lydda, and Rathamin, added to Judea from Samaria, with everything belonging to them, for all who sacrifice in Jerusalem, in place of the royal dues that the king formerly received from them each year from the produce of the land and the fruit trees.

verses.text: The other things belonging to us from now on—the tithes and dues belonging to us, the salt lakes, and the crown payments belonging to us—we grant all these to them.
verses.display_text: The other things belonging to us from now on—the tithes and dues belonging to us, the salt lakes, and the crown payments belonging to us—we grant all these to them.

verses.text: Not one of these provisions shall be annulled from now and for all time.
verses.display_text: Not one of these provisions shall be annulled from now and for all time.

verses.text: Now, therefore, take care to make a copy of these things. Let it be given to Jonathan and placed on the holy mountain in a conspicuous place.’”
verses.display_text: Now, therefore, take care to make a copy of these things. Let it be given to Jonathan and placed on the holy mountain in a conspicuous place.’”

verses.text: King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him and that nothing resisted him. He dismissed all his forces, each to his own place, except the foreign forces he had recruited from the islands of the nations. All the forces inherited from his fathers became hostile to him.
verses.display_text: King Demetrius saw that the land was quiet before him and that nothing resisted him. He dismissed all his forces, each to his own place, except the foreign forces he had recruited from the islands of the nations. All the forces inherited from his fathers became hostile to him.

verses.text: Tryphon had formerly been one of Alexander’s men. He saw that all the forces were grumbling against Demetrius and went to Imalcue the Arab, who was bringing up Alexander’s young son Antiochus.
verses.display_text: Tryphon had formerly been one of Alexander’s men. He saw that all the forces were grumbling against Demetrius and went to Imalcue the Arab, who was bringing up Alexander’s young son Antiochus.

verses.text: He stayed with him, urging him to hand the boy over so that he might reign in his father’s place. He reported everything Demetrius had done and the hostility his forces felt toward him, and remained there many days.
verses.display_text: He stayed with him, urging him to hand the boy over so that he might reign in his father’s place. He reported everything Demetrius had done and the hostility his forces felt toward him, and remained there many days.

verses.text: Jonathan sent to King Demetrius, asking him to remove the men of the citadel from Jerusalem and those in the strongholds, because they were fighting Israel.
verses.display_text: Jonathan sent to King Demetrius, asking him to remove the men of the citadel from Jerusalem and those in the strongholds, because they were fighting Israel.

verses.text: Demetrius sent to Jonathan, saying, “I will do not only these things for you and your nation, but I will greatly honour you and your nation if I find an opportunity.
verses.display_text: Demetrius sent to Jonathan, saying, “I will do not only these things for you and your nation, but I will greatly honour you and your nation if I find an opportunity.

verses.text: Now, therefore, you will do well to send me men who will fight alongside me, because all my forces have revolted.”
verses.display_text: Now, therefore, you will do well to send me men who will fight alongside me, because all my forces have revolted.”

verses.text: Jonathan sent three thousand men mighty in strength to him at Antioch. They came to the king, and the king rejoiced at their arrival.
verses.display_text: Jonathan sent three thousand men mighty in strength to him at Antioch. They came to the king, and the king rejoiced at their arrival.

verses.text: The people of the city gathered in its midst, about a hundred and twenty thousand men, intending to kill the king.
verses.display_text: The people of the city gathered in its midst, about a hundred and twenty thousand men, intending to kill the king.

verses.text: The king fled into the palace. The people of the city seized its passageways and began fighting.
verses.display_text: The king fled into the palace. The people of the city seized its passageways and began fighting.

verses.text: The king called the Jews to help. They all gathered to him together, spread through the city, and killed about a hundred thousand that day.
verses.display_text: The king called the Jews to help. They all gathered to him together, spread through the city, and killed about a hundred thousand that day.

verses.text: They burned the city, took many spoils that day, and saved the king.
verses.display_text: They burned the city, took many spoils that day, and saved the king.

verses.text: The people of the city saw that the Jews controlled the city as they wished. They lost courage and cried to the king with a plea, saying,

verses.text: “Give us your right hand, and let the Jews stop fighting us and the city.”
verses.display_text: “Give us your right hand, and let the Jews stop fighting us and the city.”

verses.text: They threw down their weapons and made peace. The Jews were honoured before the king and before everyone in his kingdom, and returned to Jerusalem with many spoils.
verses.display_text: They threw down their weapons and made peace. The Jews were honoured before the king and before everyone in his kingdom, and returned to Jerusalem with many spoils.

verses.text: King Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.
verses.display_text: King Demetrius sat upon the throne of his kingdom, and the land was quiet before him.

verses.text: He proved false in everything he had said, became estranged from Jonathan, did not repay the goodwill shown to him, and oppressed him greatly.
verses.display_text: He proved false in everything he had said, became estranged from Jonathan, did not repay the goodwill shown to him, and oppressed him greatly.

verses.text: After this Tryphon returned, and with him Antiochus, a young boy. Antiochus became king and put on a diadem.
verses.display_text: After this Tryphon returned, and with him Antiochus, a young boy. Antiochus became king and put on a diadem.

verses.display_text: All the forces Demetrius had dismissed gathered to him. They fought Demetrius, and he fled and was routed.

verses.text: Tryphon took the elephants and gained control of Antioch.
verses.display_text: Tryphon took the elephants and gained control of Antioch.

verses.text: The young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying, “I confirm you in the high priesthood, appoint you over the four districts, and make you one of the king’s Friends.”
verses.display_text: The young Antiochus wrote to Jonathan, saying, “I confirm you in the high priesthood, appoint you over the four districts, and make you one of the king’s Friends.”

verses.display_text: He sent him gold vessels and a table service, and granted him authority to drink from gold vessels, wear purple, and have a golden clasp.

verses.display_text: He appointed Simon his brother general from the Ladder of Tyre to the borders of Egypt.

verses.text: Jonathan went out and travelled through Beyond the River and its cities. All the Syrian forces gathered to him as allies. He came to Ascalon, and the people of the city met him with honour.
verses.display_text: Jonathan went out and travelled through Beyond the River and its cities. All the Syrian forces gathered to him as allies. He came to Ascalon, and the people of the city met him with honour.

verses.text: He went from there to Gaza, but the people of Gaza shut him out. He besieged it, burned its surrounding towns with fire, and plundered them.
verses.display_text: He went from there to Gaza, but the people of Gaza shut him out. He besieged it, burned its surrounding towns with fire, and plundered them.

verses.display_text: The people of Gaza appealed to Jonathan. He gave them his right hand, took their rulers’ sons as hostages, and sent them to Jerusalem. He passed through the country as far as Damascus.

verses.display_text: Jonathan heard that Demetrius’s commanders had arrived at Kedesh in Galilee with a large force, intending to remove him from his office.

verses.text: Simon encamped against Beth-zur, attacked it for many days, and blockaded it.

verses.text: “Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders of the nation, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, to the Spartans their brothers, greetings.
verses.display_text: “Jonathan the high priest, the council of elders of the nation, the priests, and the rest of the Jewish people, to the Spartans their brothers, greetings.

verses.display_text: In former times letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Areus, who reigned among you, stating that you are our brothers, as the copy below shows.

verses.text: Although we have no need of these things, since we have as encouragement the holy books that are in our hands,

verses.text: we have undertaken to send to renew brotherhood and friendship with you, so that we may not become estranged from you. For many seasons have passed since you sent to us.
verses.display_text: we have undertaken to send to renew brotherhood and friendship with you, so that we may not become estranged from you. For many seasons have passed since you sent to us.

verses.display_text: We therefore remember you continually at every season, at the festivals and the other appointed days, in the sacrifices we offer and in our prayers, as it is right and fitting to remember brothers.

verses.display_text: We rejoice in your glory.

verses.text: But many afflictions and many wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have made war on us.
verses.display_text: But many afflictions and many wars have surrounded us, and the kings around us have made war on us.

verses.text: We did not wish to trouble you or our other allies and friends in these wars,
verses.display_text: We did not wish to trouble you or our other allies and friends in these wars,

verses.display_text: for we have help from Heaven helping us; we were rescued from our enemies, and our enemies were humbled.

verses.text: We have therefore chosen Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason and sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.
verses.display_text: We have therefore chosen Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason and sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.

verses.display_text: Now you will do well to answer us concerning these matters.”

verses.text: “Areus king of the Spartans to Onias the great priest, greetings.
verses.display_text: “Areus king of the Spartans to Onias the great priest, greetings.

verses.display_text: Now that we have learned these things, you will do well to write to us concerning your welfare.

verses.display_text: We in turn write to you: your livestock and your property are ours, and ours are yours. We therefore command that they report to you accordingly.”

verses.display_text: Jonathan heard that Demetrius’s commanders had returned with a force larger than before to fight him.

verses.display_text: He set out from Jerusalem and met them in the region of Hamath, for he gave them no opportunity to enter his country.

verses.display_text: He sent spies into their camp. They returned and reported to him that they were arranging to fall upon them that night.

verses.display_text: When the sun went down, Jonathan commanded his men to keep watch and remain under arms, ready for battle all night. He posted sentries around the camp.

verses.text: and raising Jerusalem’s walls higher, and building a great barrier between the citadel and the city to separate it from the city, so that it might stand alone and its people could neither buy nor sell.

verses.display_text: He feared that Jonathan might not permit him and might fight against him. He sought to seize and destroy him, and set out and came to Beth-shan.

verses.display_text: Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand picked men for battle, and came to Beth-shan.

verses.text: Tryphon saw that he had come with a large force and feared to stretch out his hands against him.
verses.display_text: Tryphon saw that he had come with a large force and feared to stretch out his hands against him.

verses.text: He received him with honour, introduced him to all his Friends, gave him gifts, and commanded his Friends and forces to obey him as they obeyed himself.
verses.display_text: He received him with honour, introduced him to all his Friends, gave him gifts, and commanded his Friends and forces to obey him as they obeyed himself.

verses.display_text: He said to Jonathan, “Why have you wearied all these people when no war threatens us?

verses.display_text: Jonathan trusted him and did as he said. He sent away the forces, and they departed to the land of Judah.

verses.display_text: When Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the people of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him. They killed with the sword everyone who had entered with him.

verses.display_text: Tryphon sent forces and cavalry into Galilee and the great plain to destroy all Jonathan’s men.

verses.display_text: They learned that he had been captured and had perished, along with those with him. They encouraged one another and marched in close formation, ready for battle.

verses.display_text: Their pursuers saw that they were fighting for their lives and turned back.

verses.display_text: They all came safely into the land of Judah, mourned Jonathan and those with him, and were exceedingly afraid. All Israel mourned with great mourning.

verses.display_text: All the nations around them sought to crush them, for they said, “They have no ruler or helper. Now let us fight them and remove their memory from among humankind.”

verses.display_text: Simon heard that Tryphon had gathered a large force to enter the land of Judah and crush it.

verses.display_text: He saw that the people were trembling and terrified. He went up to Jerusalem and gathered the people.

verses.display_text: He encouraged them and said, “You yourselves know all that I, my brothers, and my father’s house have done for the laws and the holy places, and the battles and hardships we have seen.

verses.text: For this cause all my brothers have perished for Israel, and I alone am left.
verses.display_text: For this cause all my brothers have perished for Israel, and I alone am left.

verses.display_text: Now far be it from me to spare my life in any time of distress, for I am no better than my brothers.

verses.display_text: I will avenge my nation, the holy places, your wives, and your children, for all the nations have gathered to crush us out of hatred.”

verses.display_text: The spirit of the people was rekindled as soon as they heard these words.

verses.text: They answered in a loud voice, saying, “You are our leader in place of Judas and Jonathan your brother.
verses.display_text: They answered in a loud voice, saying, “You are our leader in place of Judas and Jonathan your brother.

verses.text: Fight our war, and we will do everything you tell us.”
verses.display_text: Fight our war, and we will do everything you tell us.”

verses.text: He gathered all the warriors, hastened to complete Jerusalem’s walls, and fortified it all around.
verses.display_text: He gathered all the warriors, hastened to complete Jerusalem’s walls, and fortified it all around.

verses.display_text: He sent Jonathan son of Absalom and a sufficient force with him to Joppa. He expelled those who were in it and remained there.

verses.display_text: Tryphon set out from Ptolemais with a large force to enter the land of Judah, with Jonathan under guard.

verses.display_text: “We are holding Jonathan your brother because of money he owed to the royal treasury for the offices he held.

verses.display_text: Now send a hundred talents of silver and two of his sons as hostages, so that he will not revolt against us when released, and we will release him.”

verses.display_text: Simon knew that they were speaking deceitfully to him, yet sent to fetch the money and the children, lest he incur great hostility among the people

verses.display_text: Tryphon dealt deceitfully with the young King Antiochus and killed him.

verses.display_text: Simon rebuilt Judea’s strongholds, enclosed them with high towers and great walls, gates, and bars, and placed food in the strongholds.

verses.display_text: Simon chose men and sent them to King Demetrius to secure remission for the country, because all Tryphon’s acts were plunder.

verses.display_text: Antiochus son of King Demetrius sent letters from the islands of the sea to Simon, priest and ethnarch of the Jews, and to the whole nation.

verses.display_text: They contained the following: “King Antiochus to Simon the great priest and ethnarch, and to the nation of the Jews, greetings.

verses.text: Since certain pestilent men have seized the kingdom of our fathers, I wish to reclaim the kingdom and restore it as it was before. I have recruited a multitude of forces and prepared warships.
verses.display_text: Since certain pestilent men have seized the kingdom of our fathers, I wish to reclaim the kingdom and restore it as it was before. I have recruited a multitude of forces and prepared warships.

verses.text: I intend to land in the country to pursue those who have ruined our country and devastated many cities in my kingdom.
verses.display_text: I intend to land in the country to pursue those who have ruined our country and devastated many cities in my kingdom.

verses.text: Now, therefore, I confirm to you all the remissions that the kings before me granted you, and all the other gifts they granted you.
verses.display_text: Now, therefore, I confirm to you all the remissions that the kings before me granted you, and all the other gifts they granted you.

verses.display_text: I permit you to strike your own coinage as money for your country.

verses.text: Jerusalem and the holy places shall be free. All the weapons you have prepared and the strongholds you have built and hold shall remain yours.

verses.text: Every royal debt and all future royal dues shall be remitted to you from now and for all time.
verses.display_text: Every royal debt and all future royal dues shall be remitted to you from now and for all time.

verses.text: When we gain control of our kingdom, we will honour you, your nation, and the temple with great glory, so that your glory may become evident throughout the whole earth.”
verses.display_text: When we gain control of our kingdom, we will honour you, your nation, and the temple with great glory, so that your glory may become evident throughout the whole earth.”

verses.display_text: In the one hundred and seventy-fourth year Antiochus went out into the land of his fathers. All the forces joined him, so that only a few remained with Tryphon.

verses.text: Someone ran ahead and reported to John at Gazara that his father and brothers had perished, and said, “He has also sent men to kill you.”

verses.text: When he heard, he was greatly astonished. He seized the men who had come to destroy him and killed them, for he had learned that they were seeking to destroy him.
